limits: These are independent model-review judgments, not human ground truth and not evidence of causal instruction use.
Compatibility means the actual segment is observably consistent with the full cited source fragment in the supplied task context.
Contradicted means the emitted relation is false or the segment violates the cited rule under an explicit task requirement.
Insufficient-evidence preserves absence-based, baseline-dependent, or otherwise undecidable claims.
Prompt-supplied React terms can support observable compatibility but cannot distinguish prompt influence from skill influence.
The case applicability map was treated as a prior, not as a semantic oracle.

rubric.literal: Require a meaningful shared phrase or construction, not merely a valid ID, copied source quote, or generic/common token.
rubric.rule_compatibility: Require an independently checkable task fact such as exact required artifacts, explicit polarity, explicit output language, or persisted-artifact prose. Failure of an explicit requirement contradicts an exactness claim.
rubric.omission: Count only an un-emitted relationship that the same rubric can positively establish. Do not call an absent ID a causal false negative.
rubric.uncertainty: Use insufficient-evidence for no-caricature, growth-versus-baseline, and generic language/style claims lacking enough context.

coverage.sampling: none; every emitted link and every tagged response/segment was inspected
